answer:
**The meta-analysis** (pooled RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE, ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48; 71,683 participants — 42,411 on a new oral anticoagulant, 29,272 on warfarin) concludes, versus warfarin:

- **Stroke or systemic embolism:** reduced 19% (RR 0·81, 95% CI 0·73–0·91; p<0·0001), mainly driven by the haemorrhagic stroke reduction.
- **Haemorrhagic stroke:** RR 0·49 (0·38–0·64; p<0·0001).
- **All-cause mortality:** RR 0·90 (0·85–0·95; p=0·0003).
- **Intracranial haemorrhage:** RR 0·48 (0·39–0·59; p<0·0001).
- **Gastrointestinal bleeding:** *increased*, RR 1·25 (1·01–1·55; p=0·04).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"New oral anticoagulants significantly reduced stroke or systemic embolic events by 19% compared with warfarin (RR 0·81, 95% CI 0·73-0·91; p<0·0001), mainly driven by a reduction in haemorrhagic stroke (0·49, 0·38-0·64; p<0·0001). New oral anticoagulants also significantly reduced all-cause mortality (0·90, 0·85-0·95; p=0·0003) and intracranial haemorrhage (0·48, 0·39-0·59; p<0·0001), but increased gastrointestinal bleeding (1·25, 1·01-1·55; p=0·04)."}) -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"We did a prespecified meta-analysis of all 71,683 participants included in the RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE, and ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 trials."}) -->
Condition-dependent caveats: the major-bleeding benefit was greater where centre-based time in therapeutic range was <66% (0·69, 0·59–0·81) than ≥66% (0·93, 0·76–1·13; p for interaction 0·022); low-dose regimens gave no significant reduction in stroke/systemic embolism (1·03, 0·84–1·27; p=0·74) and significantly more ischaemic strokes (1·28, 1·02–1·60; p=0·045).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"Low-dose new oral anticoagulant regimens showed similar overall reductions in stroke or systemic embolic events to warfarin (1·03, 0·84-1·27; p=0·74), and a more favourable bleeding profile (0·65, 0·43-1·00; p=0·05), but significantly more ischaemic strokes (1·28, 1·02-1·60; p=0·045)."}) -->

**Consistency with the individual trials' own reports:**

- **RE-LY (dabigatran):** haemorrhagic stroke 0·38%/year with warfarin vs 0·12%/year with 110 mg (P<0·001) and 0·10%/year with 150 mg (P<0·001) — i.e. a large relative reduction, consistent in direction with the pooled RR 0·49.

answer:
**Short answer:** the benefit on cardiovascular death alone is smaller and less robust than the benefit on heart failure hospitalization; it was statistically significant in DAPA-HF, not significant in DELIVER, and in EMPEROR-Preserved the effect was "mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure."

**DAPA-HF** (HFrEF, EF ≤40%, n=4744, median 18.2 months): cardiovascular death occurred in 227 (9.6%) vs 273 (11.5%), HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98) — a significant reduction, alongside first worsening heart failure HR 0.70 (0.59–0.83) and all-cause death HR 0.83 (0.71–0.97).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)"} -->

**EMPEROR-Preserved** (EF >40%, n=5988, median 26.2 months): primary composite HR 0.79 (0.69–0.90), but "This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group"; total HF hospitalizations HR 0.73 (0.61–0.88). No separate cardiovascular death hazard ratio is reported in this document.

**DELIVER** (EF >40%, n=6263, median 2.3 years): primary composite HR 0.82 (0.73–0.92); worsening HF HR 0.79 (0.69–0.91); cardiovascular death 231 (7.4%) vs 261 (8.3%), HR 0.88 (0.74–1.05) — not statistically significant.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05)"} -->

**Meta-analysis (five trials, 21,947 participants):** in the HFmrEF/HFpEF pair (DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved, n=12,251) cardiovascular death HR was 0.88 (0.77–1.00) — borderline, touching 1.00 — versus HF hospitalization 0.74 (0.67–0.83). Across all five trials, cardiovascular death HR 0.87 (0.79–0.95), HF hospitalization 0.72 (0.67–0.78), all-cause mortality 0.92 (0.86–0.99).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00]) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·74 [0·67-0·83])"} -->

So: a significant stand-alone cardiovascular mortality reduction is documented only for DAPA-HF (reduced EF); in the preserved-EF trials the mortality component was not clearly reduced on its own, and the meta-analysis finds a modest, less certain effect on cardiovascular death than on heart failure hospitalization.

**DAPA-HF (reduced EF): yes, on its own.** Cardiovascular death occurred in 227 (9.6%) on dapagliflozin vs 273 (11.5%) on placebo, HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98); all-cause death 11.6% vs 13.9%, HR 0.83 (0.71–0.97) — in patients with HF and EF ≤40%.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)"} -->

**DELIVER (mildly reduced/preserved EF): no — the benefit was driven by worsening HF.** The primary composite (worsening HF or CV death) fell (16.4% vs 19.5%, HR 0.82, 0.73–0.92; P<0.001), and worsening HF fell (11.8% vs 14.5%, HR 0.79, 0.69–0.91), but CV death alone was not significantly reduced: 231 (7.4%) vs 261 (8.3%), HR 0.88 (0.74–1.05).

**Meta-analysis (five trials, 21,947 participants):** CV death was reduced overall — HR 0.87 (0.79–0.95), along with the composite (0.77, 0.72–0.82), first HF hospitalization (0.72, 0.67–0.78) and all-cause mortality (0.92, 0.86–0.99). (SGLT-2 inhibitors in patients with heart failure: a comprehensive meta-analysis of five randomised controlled trials)
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"In the broader context of the five trials of 21 947 participants, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of composite cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure (0·77 [0·72-0·82])"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"Treatment effects on the primary endpoint were generally consistent across the 14 subgroups examined, including ejection fraction."} -->

Note: the composite definitions differ slightly (DAPA-HF and DELIVER include worsening HF as urgent visit/hospitalization; the EMPEROR trials use CV death or HF hospitalization), so the hazard ratios are not strictly like-for-like.

**Short answer:** the benefit on cardiovascular death alone is smaller and less robust than the benefit on heart failure hospitalization; it was statistically significant in DAPA-HF, not significant in DELIVER, and in EMPEROR-Preserved the effect was "mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure."

**DAPA-HF** (HFrEF, EF ≤40%, n=4744, median 18.2 months): cardiovascular death occurred in 227 (9.6%) vs 273 (11.5%), HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98) — a significant reduction, alongside first worsening heart failure HR 0.70 (0.59–0.83) and all-cause death HR 0.83 (0.71–0.97).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)"} -->

**EMPEROR-Preserved** (EF >40%, n=5988, median 26.2 months): primary composite HR 0.79 (0.69–0.90), but "This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group"; total HF hospitalizations HR 0.73 (0.61–0.88). No separate cardiovascular death hazard ratio is reported in this document.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group."} -->

**DELIVER** (EF >40%, n=6263, median 2.3 years): primary composite HR 0.82 (0.73–0.92); worsening HF HR 0.79 (0.69–0.91); cardiovascular death 231 (7.4%) vs 261 (8.3%), HR 0.88 (0.74–1.05) — not statistically significant.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05)"} -->

**Meta-analysis (five trials, 21,947 participants):** in the HFmrEF/HFpEF pair (DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved, n=12,251) cardiovascular death HR was 0.88 (0.77–1.00) — borderline, touching 1.00 — versus HF hospitalization 0.74 (0.67–0.83). Across all five trials, cardiovascular death HR 0.87 (0.79–0.95), HF hospitalization 0.72 (0.67–0.78), all-cause mortality 0.92 (0.86–0.99).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00]) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·74 [0·67-0·83])"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"cardiovascular death (0·87 [0·79-0·95]), first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·72 [0·67-0·78]), and all-cause mortality (0·92 [0·86-0·99])"} -->

So: a significant stand-alone cardiovascular mortality reduction is documented only for DAPA-HF (reduced EF); in the preserved-EF trials the mortality component was not clearly reduced on its own, and the meta-analysis finds a modest, less certain effect on cardiovascular death than on heart failure hospitalization.

**DAPA-HF (reduced EF): yes, on its own.** Cardiovascular death occurred in 227 (9.6%) on dapagliflozin vs 273 (11.5%) on placebo, HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98); all-cause death 11.6% vs 13.9%, HR 0.83 (0.71–0.97) — in patients with HF and EF ≤40%.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)"} -->

**DELIVER (mildly reduced/preserved EF): no — the benefit was driven by worsening HF.** The primary composite (worsening HF or CV death) fell (16.4% vs 19.5%, HR 0.82, 0.73–0.92; P<0.001), and worsening HF fell (11.8% vs 14.5%, HR 0.79, 0.69–0.91), but CV death alone was not significantly reduced: 231 (7.4%) vs 261 (8.3%), HR 0.88 (0.74–1.05).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05)"} -->

**EMPEROR-Preserved (EF >40%):** the reported result is for the composite of CV death or hospitalization for HF (19.4% vs 24.7%, HR 0.75, 0.65–0.86; P<0.001); the documents available here do not give a separate CV-death hazard ratio for this trial.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_b5b2f2860d0e0ed2b6663cb104221791","quote":"a primary outcome event occurred in 361 of 1863 patients (19.4%) in the empagliflozin group and in 462 of 1867 patients (24.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001)"} -->

**Meta-analysis (five trials, 21,947 participants):** CV death was reduced overall — HR 0.87 (0.79–0.95), along with the composite (0.77, 0.72–0.82), first HF hospitalization (0.72, 0.67–0.78) and all-cause mortality (0.92, 0.86–0.99). But in the preserved-EF pair alone (DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved, 12,251 participants), the CV-death reduction was borderline: 0.88 (0.77–1.00), versus a clear 0.74 (0.67–0.83) for first HF hospitalization.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of composite cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure (0·77 [0·72-0·82]), cardiovascular death (0·87 [0·79-0·95]), first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·72 [0·67-0·78]), and all-cause mortality (0·92 [0·86-0·99])"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"with consistent reductions in both components: cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00]) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·74 [0·67-0·83])"} -->

So: a genuine stand-alone CV-mortality benefit is documented in reduced EF (DAPA-HF) and in the pooled five-trial analysis, whereas in preserved EF the mortality effect is not clearly separated from the hospitalization/worsening-HF benefit.

All four sources agree that aspirin raises bleeding in people without established cardiovascular disease.

**ASCEND** (diabetes, no evident CVD; aspirin 100 mg/day, mean follow-up 7.4 years): major bleeding events in 314 (4.1%) vs 245 (3.2%), rate ratio 1.29 (95% CI 1.09–1.52; P=0.003), mostly gastrointestinal and other extracranial bleeding, against a reduction in serious vascular events (8.5% vs 9.6%; RR 0.88). - Harm: increased major bleeding — 23.1 vs 16.4 per 10,000 participant-years; HR 1.43 (1.30–1.56); absolute risk increase 0.47% (0.34%–0.62%); NNH 210. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_64f23983bfe8fd167aa6725f288d7375","quote":"23.1 per 10 000 participant-years with aspirin and 16.4 per 10 000 participant-years with no aspirin) (HR, 1.43 [95% credible interval, 1.30-1.56]"}} -->

**The meta-analysis (Lancet 2014, 71,683 participants across RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE and ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48):** compared with warfarin, the new oral anticoagulants significantly reduced stroke or systemic embolic events by 19% (RR 0·81, 95% CI 0·73–0·91; p<0·0001), mainly driven by a reduction in haemorrhagic stroke (0·49, 0·38–0·64; p<0·0001), and also reduced all-cause mortality (0·90, 0·85–0·95; p=0·0003) and intracranial haemorrhage (0·48, 0·39–0·59; p<0·0001), but increased gastrointestinal bleeding (1·25, 1·01–1·55; p=0·04).

**Consistency with the individual trials:** yes, the direction and magnitude match. In ARISTOTLE, haemorrhagic stroke was 0.24%/year with apixaban vs 0.47%/year with warfarin (HR 0.51; 95% CI 0.35–0.75; P<0.001) — essentially the pooled 0·49 estimate.

- **Why it ended early:** the data and safety monitoring board recommended early termination because of a clear benefit in favor of apixaban.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405","quote":"The data and safety monitoring board recommended early termination of the study because of a clear benefit in favor of apixaban."} -->

- **DAPA-HF** (HFrEF, median 18.2 months): 16.3% vs 21.2%, HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.65–0.85), P<0.001 — Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001"} -->
- **EMPEROR-Reduced** (HFrEF, median 16 months): 19.4% vs 24.7%, HR 0.75 (0.65–0.86), P<0.001 — Cardiovascular and Renal Outcomes with Empagliflozin in Heart Failure. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_b5b2f2860d0e0ed2b6663cb104221791","quote":"hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001"} -->
- **EMPEROR-Preserved** (HFmrEF/HFpEF, median 26.2 months): 13.8% vs 17.1%, HR 0.79 (0.69–0.90), P<0.001, driven mainly by fewer HF hospitalizations — Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.90; P<0.001"} -->
- **DELIVER** (HFmrEF/HFpEF, median 2.3 years): 16.4% vs 19.5%, HR 0.82 (0.73–0.92), P<0.001 — Dapagliflozin in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.92; P<0.001"} -->

Across the ejection fraction range: in the meta-analysis of all five trials (21,947 participants), the composite of CV death or HF hospitalization was reduced to HR 0.77 (0.72–0.82), and treatment effects were consistent in the HFmrEF/HFpEF trials and across all five trials, with the primary-endpoint effect generally consistent across 14 subgroups including ejection fraction (SGLT-2 inhibitors in patients with heart failure: a comprehensive meta-analysis of five randomised controlled trials). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of composite cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure (0·77 [0·72-0·82])"} --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"Treatment effects on the primary endpoint were generally consistent across the 14 subgroups examined, including ejection fraction." -->

Note: the individual trial reports do not give per-trial data on the ejection fraction continuum; the consistency statement rests on the meta-analysis, which used harmonised endpoint definitions and trial-level data.

**Kidney function (eGFR entry):**
- CREDENCE: eGFR 30 to <90 ml/min/1.73 m², all with albuminuria and on RAS blockade. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"All the patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 30 to <90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and albuminuria (ratio of albumin [mg] to creatinine [g], >300 to 5000)"} -->
- DAPA-CKD: eGFR 25 to 75 ml/min/1.73 m² (4304 participants). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"We randomly assigned 4304 participants with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 25 to 75 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area"} -->
- EMPA-KIDNEY: broader, two-pathway entry — eGFR ≥20 to <45, or eGFR ≥45 to <90 with UACR ≥200. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of at least 20 but less than 45 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area, or who had an eGFR of at least 45 but less than 90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 with a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio" -->

**Albuminuria:** CREDENCE required UACR >300 to 5000 mg/g; DAPA-CKD required 200 to 5000 mg/g; EMPA-KIDNEY required UACR ≥200 only for those with eGFR 45 to <90 (no albuminuria threshold for eGFR <45). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (with albumin measured in milligrams and creatinine in grams) of 200 to 5000"} --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"with a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (with albumin measured in milligrams and creatinine in grams) of at least 200"} -->

**Diabetes status:** CREDENCE enrolled only patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric CKD; DAPA-CKD and EMPA-KIDNEY enrolled patients with or without diabetes. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"we assigned patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease to receive canagliflozin"} --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"The effect of dapagliflozin in patients with chronic kidney disease, with or without type 2 diabetes, is not known."} -->

**Consistency with and without diabetes:**
- DAPA-CKD: effects similar in participants with and without type 2 diabetes; benefit regardless of diabetes presence. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"The effects of dapagliflozin were similar in participants with type 2 diabetes and in those without type 2 diabetes."} -->
- EMPA-KIDNEY: results consistent among patients with or without diabetes and across eGFR subgroups. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"Results were consistent among patients with or without diabetes and across subgroups defined according to eGFR ranges."} -->
- CREDENCE: by design all participants had type 2 diabetes, so no diabetes-free comparison exists in that trial. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"In patients with type 2 diabetes and kidney disease, the risk of kidney failure and cardiovascular events was lower in the canagliflozin group than in the placebo group"} -->
